He was a two-time [[NBA All-Star]] and was named to the [[NBA All-Defensive Second Team]] in 2012. Born in [[South Sudan]], then part of [[Republic of Sudan (1985–2019)|Sudan]], Deng fled the country with his family as a child, eventually settling in the [[United Kingdom]]. He became a [[British citizen]] in 2006, and has played for the [[Great Britain men's national basketball team|Great Britain national team]]. After playing [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]], Deng was selected by the [[Phoenix Suns]] in the first round of the [[2004 NBA draft]] with the seventh overall pick. He was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]] as a 19-year-old in 2005. The [[small forward]] was an All-Star with the Bulls in 2012 and 2013 before splitting the 2013–14 season with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. After just half a season with Cleveland, Deng joined the [[Miami Heat]] for 2014–15. He played two seasons for the Heat before signing with the Lakers in 2016. He spent his last season with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. Deng has been the president of the [[South Sudan Basketball Federation]] since 2019. He is an assistant coach for the [[South Sudan men's national basketball team]] and has previously served as its head coach. ==Early life== Deng was born in [[Wau, South Sudan|Wau]], [[Republic of Sudan (1985–2019)|Sudan]] (present-day [[South Sudan]]), and is a member of the [[Dinka people|Dinka]] ethnic group. When he was young, his father [[Aldo Deng|Aldo]], a member of the Sudanese parliament, moved the family to [[Egypt]] to escape the [[Second Sudanese Civil War]].{{Cite web |url= http://www.nba.com/playerfile/luol_deng/bio.html |title=Luol Deng | website= NBA.com |access-date=29 December 2006 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080801100507/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/luol_deng/bio.html |archive-date=1 August 2008 |url-status=dead}} In Egypt, they met former NBA player [[Manute Bol]], another Dinka, who taught Deng's older brother, [[Ajou Deng]], how to play basketball and also mentored Luol.{{Cite web |url= http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/rookies_040830.html |title=BULLS: Triple Threat |website= NBA.com |access-date=4 November 2006 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20060827130237/http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/rookies_040830.html |archive-date=27 August 2006 |url-status=live}}{{cite news | url= https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2005/apr/03/ussport.features | work=The Guardian | location=London | title=Triumph and despair: Luol Deng | date=3 April 2005 | access-date=11 May 2010 | first=Sam | last=Pilger | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080122200828/http://observer.guardian.co.uk/osm/story/0,,1448493,00.html | archive-date=22 January 2008 | url-status=live | df=dmy-all}} When they were granted political asylum, his family immigrated to [[Brixton]] in [[South London]]. Deng was educated at [[St Mary's Roman Catholic High School, Croydon|St Mary's Roman Catholic High School]],{{Cite news |url= https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/olympic_games/world_olympic_dreams/8859096.stm |title=St. Mary's Catholic High School, Great Britain| website= news.bbc.co.uk |date=28 July 2010 |access-date=3 March 2015 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20150402122526/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/olympic_games/world_olympic_dreams/8859096.stm |archive-date=2 April 2015 |url-status= live }} a [[Voluntary aided school|voluntary aided]] state comprehensive school in [[Croydon]] in South London. He developed an interest in [[Association football|football]], admiring [[Faustino Asprilla]] of [[Newcastle United F.C.]],{{Cite web | last = Douglas | first = Mark | title = Tino was hero to me, reveals Deng | work = Evening Chronicle | date = 3 August 2010 | url = http://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/sport/basketball-news/newcastle-eagles/2010/08/03/tino-was-hero-to-me-reveals-deng-72703-26985331/ | access-date= 3 August 2010 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120404031653/http://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/sport/basketball-news/newcastle-eagles/2010/08/03/tino-was-hero-to-me-reveals-deng-72703-26985331/ | archive-date = 4 April 2012 | url-status = live | df = dmy-all }} but also continued to play basketball and was invited to join England's under-15 team. During this time, he began his career at the [[Brixton TopCats]]. At Brixton, Deng was coached by [[Jimmy Rogers (basketball, born 1939)|Jimmy Rogers]], who convinced him to play basketball.{{Cite news |last=Lewis |first=Tim |date=2018-10-06 |title=Farewell to father of British basketball who discovered Luol Deng |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/blog/2018/oct/06/farewell-to-father-of-british-basketball-who-discovered-luol-deng |access-date=2024-11-02 |work=The Guardian |issn=0261-3077}} He represented [[London Borough of Croydon|Croydon]] at the [[London Youth Games]] and was inducted into their Hall of Fame.{{cite news | url=http://www.suttonguardian.co.uk/sport/4640269.Basketball_hero_Deng_so_proud_of_Croydon_roots/?ref=rss | work= Sutton Guardian | title=Luol Deng's delight at London Youth Games honour | date=23 September 2009 | first=Graham | last= Moody | location=London | access-date=19 March 2012 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20130606014434/http://www.suttonguardian.co.uk/sport/4640269.Basketball_hero_Deng_so_proud_of_Croydon_roots/?ref=rss | archive-date=6 June 2013 | url-status=live | df= dmy-all}} At age 13, he played for the [[England men's national under-18 basketball team|England under-18 team]] in the [[1998 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]] qualifying tournament, averaging 40 points and 14 rebounds, and was named the most valuable player (MVP) of the tournament.{{citation needed|date=November 2024}} Next, he led [[England]] to the finals of the European Junior National Tournament, where he averaged (34) points and earned another MVP award.{{citation needed|date=November 2024}} At age 14, Deng moved to the [[United States]] to play [[basketball]] at [[Blair Academy]] in [[New Jersey]]. One of his teammates was future NBA player [[Charlie Villanueva]]. Deng was also named a tri-captain at Blair along with Villanueva. During his senior year, Deng was considered the second most promising high school senior in the United States after [[LeBron James]] and was named First Team All-America by ''[[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|Parade]]'' and [[USA Today]]. He was selected to play in the McDonald's High School All-America game, but could not play due to a foot injury.{{cite news| url= http://chronicle.augusta.com/stories/032703/pre_124-4178.shtml | title= LeBron leads East to victory| agency= [[Associated Press|AP]] | work= [[Augusta Chronicle]] | date= 27 March 2003}}{{cite web| url= http://www.basketball365.co.uk/mcdonalds260303.htm | title= Luol Deng sidelined for McDonalds All-American game| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20081121184723/http://www.basketball365.co.uk/mcdonalds260303.htm |archive-date=21 November 2008 | work= Basketball365.co.uk | date= 26 March 2003}} Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Deng was listed as the no. 1 small forward and the no. 2 player in the nation in 2003.{{cite web| url= https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Luol-Deng-4528 | title=Luol Deng Recruiting Profile| website= sports.yahoo.com | publisher=Yahoo}} ==College career== Deng accepted an athletic scholarship to attend [[Duke University]], where he played for coach [[Mike Krzyzewski]]'s [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils basketball]] team in [[2003–04 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|2003–04]]. In one season at Duke, he appeared in 37 games and made 32 starts. He averaged 30.1 minutes and 15.1 [[points per game]] en route to a berth in the [[2004 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2004 Final Four]]. He was the 10th freshman in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) history to lead all freshmen in scoring, rebounding, and field goal percentage.{{citation needed|date=November 2024}} ==Professional career== ===Chicago Bulls (2004–2014)=== ====2004–05 season==== After one year at Duke, Deng entered the [[2004 NBA draft]]. He was picked seventh overall by the [[Phoenix Suns]], but was immediately traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] by prior agreement. Deng suffered a season-ending wrist injury late in his rookie season, but still made the [[NBA All-Rookie First Team]] and helped the resurgent Bulls return to the playoffs for the first time in seven years. Deng played in 61 games and averaged 11.7 points per game. On 8 February 2005, Deng recorded his first [[double-double]] in a 107–100 win against the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/200502080DAL.html |title=Chicago Bulls at Dallas Mavericks Box Score, February 8, 2005 |publisher=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=2 December 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170620063623/http://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/200502080DAL.html |archive-date=20 June 2017 |url-status=live}} ====2005–06 season==== In his second season, he posted strong performances throughout March and April 2006, to help the Bulls earn their second consecutive playoff berth. His offensive statistics improved in his sophomore season, increasing his scoring to 14.3 points per game, and increasing his rebounding to 6.6 per game, up from a 5.3 average in his rookie season. Deng had four straight double-double performances from 28 February to 5 March, with at least 10 points and rebounds in each game. In the playoffs, the Bulls faced off against the [[Miami Heat]] in a seven-game series. Deng came off the bench in all six games, averaging 10 points per game.{{citation needed|date=November 2024}} ====2006–07 season==== For the [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07 season]], Deng was the only Bulls player to start all 82 regular season games. His statistics continued to improve, and he led the team in minutes played (37.5) and field goal percentage (.517), while playing a strong second scoring option to [[Ben Gordon (basketball)|Ben Gordon]], with a marked improvement to 18.8 points per game. Deng also notably rarely committed fouls on defense (2.00 per game), despite the minutes he played and frequently being outsized in matchups against power forwards such as [[Kevin Garnett]].{{citation needed|date=November 2024}} On 27 December 2006, Deng was driving in the lane when Miami Heat's [[James Posey]] grabbed him, causing concern that Deng may have re-injured his wrist. Posey earned a [[flagrant foul]], was ejected and suspended for one game.{{citation needed|date=November 2024}} Deng scored 32 points against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] just three nights later, resolving concern that the wrist would be re-injured. On 26 March 2007, Deng posted a new career-high 38 points to lead the Bulls to a 100–89 victory against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. Deng converted 18 of his 25 shots from the field.{{citation needed|date=November 2024}} On 3 May, Deng won the [[NBA Sportsmanship Award]]. For that award, the league donated $25,000 on his behalf to [[Pacific Garden Mission]], the oldest continuously operating rescue mission in the country.{{citation needed|date=November 2024}} ====2007–08 season==== Near the beginning of the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]], the Bulls started negotiating a contract extension with Deng. Negotiations were mostly handled by Bulls chairman [[Jerry Reinsdorf]]. The team offered Deng a five-year extension for $57.5 million. However, Deng decided to reject the deal and wait until the season ended to continue negotiations.[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3510232 At long last, Bulls announce signing of Deng to six-year deal] on [[ESPN]]; [[Marc Stein (reporter)|Stein, Marc]] (31 July 2008) In the 2007–08 season, Deng played in 63 games, missing 19 mostly because of left [[Achilles tendinitis]].[https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2008022017 Nets beat bulls in first game since trading Kidd] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305033056/https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2008022017 |date=5 March 2016 }} on [[Yahoo!]] Sports; Mahoney, Brian (20 February 2008) Despite injuries, he averaged 17.0 points per game and 6.3 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/luol_deng/career_stats.html|title=Luol Deng|work=NBA.com|access-date=30 November 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150204133437/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/luol_deng/career_stats.html|archive-date=4 February 2015}} He had his best game of the season against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] when he scored 32 points in a 151–135 victory.[https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2008041415 Deng scores 32, Gordon (29) in Bulls 151–135 offensive explosion against Bucks] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305213720/https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2008041415 |date=5 March 2016 }} on [[Yahoo!]] Sports; Fly, Colin (14 April 2008) The Bulls missed the playoffs in the 2007–08 season for the first time since 2004. ====2008–09 season==== [[File:Luol Deng Wizards.jpg|thumb|left|alt=Man wearing red Bulls uniform in pursuit of the ball|Deng with Chicago in 2009]] Before the [[2008–09 NBA season|2008–09 season]] started, Deng agreed to a contract extension for six years and $71 million.{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/other_sports/basketball/7533243.stm|title=Deng agrees £40m Chicago contract|publisher=BBC|date=30 July 2008|access-date=30 July 2008}} After the agreement was announced, Bulls general manager [[John Paxson]] said in a statement "Signing Luol has always been a priority for this organization and we have always felt that he was a big part of our future. We are very happy that Luol will now be with us long term as we continue to grow as an organization." Due to injury, Deng played in 48 games. During the regular season his scoring dropped to 14.1 points per game and his rebounding dropped to 6.0 per game. The Bulls made the playoffs, but Deng missed the [[2009 NBA playoffs|2009 playoffs]] due to injury. ====2009–10 season==== Deng played in a total of 70 games during the [[2009–10 NBA season|2009–10 season]], also increasing his scoring and rebounding to 17.6 and 7.3 respectively, helping the Bulls make the playoffs again. He missed 11 straight games at the end of March 2010, because of a sprained right calf.[https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2010040227 Healthier Bulls gain ground, beat Wizards 125–45] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140813174426/https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2010040227 |date=13 August 2014 }} on ''[[Yahoo!]]'' Sports; White, Joseph (2 April 2010) During the first round of the [[2010 NBA playoffs|2010 playoffs]], Deng averaged 18.8 points along with 5.0 rebounds per game against the Cleveland Cavaliers. He scored 26 points in the final game of the series, but could not prevent the Bulls from being eliminated by the Cavaliers.[https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2010042705 LeBron, Cavs eliminate Bulls, face Celtics next] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140813174629/https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2010042705 |date=13 August 2014 }} on ''[[Yahoo!]] Sports''; Withers, Tom (28 April 2010) ====2010–11 season==== On 1 November 2010, Deng scored a new career-high 40 points, hitting 14 of his 19 shots, along with 9 of 11 free throws, against the Portland Trail Blazers, scoring a point a minute.[https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2010110104 Deng's career-high 40 points lifts Bulls] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305071449/https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2010110104 |date=5 March 2016 }} on [[Yahoo!]] Sports (2 November 2011) On 24 February 2011, he recorded 20 points, 10 rebounds, and hit the game winning three-point shot with 16 seconds left in a game against the [[Miami Heat]].[https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2011022404 Rose, Deng lead Bulls over Heat 93–89] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304234735/https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2011022404 |date=4 March 2016 }} on [[Yahoo!]] Sports; Seligman, Andrew (25 February 2011) Throughout the season, Deng significantly improved his three-point shooting after coach [[Tom Thibodeau]] asked him to. In the past four seasons, Deng attempted 132 three-point shots, whereas during this season he attempted 333, making 115.[http://dimemag.com/2011/03/pass-the-mic-luol-deng-wins-the-most-underrated-player-award/ Pass the Mic: Luol Deng Wins The Most Underrated Player Award] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110405073141/http://dimemag.com/2011/03/pass-the-mic-luol-deng-wins-the-most-underrated-player-award/ |date=5 April 2011 }} on ''[[Dime Magazine]]''; Bressman, Eric (31 March 2011) Deng finished the season averaging 17.4 points and 5.8 rebounds per game, being the third scorer for the Bulls behind [[Derrick Rose]] (25.0) and [[Carlos Boozer]] (17.5).[https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/players/3824/career;_ylt=AjjY9aeUsQztMpaMkXAtiAD4PKB4 Luol Deng – Chicago Bulls – Career Statistics] on [[Yahoo!]] Sports During the first round of the [[2011 NBA playoffs|2011 playoffs]] against the [[Indiana Pacers]], Deng averaged 18.6 points and 6.2 rebounds per game, being the second leading scorer of the team behind Derrick Rose. On 31 March 2011, Eric Bressman of ''[[Dime Magazine|Dime]]'' magazine called Deng "the most underrated player" writing he was "never the face of the franchise but always the backbone".[http://dimemag.com/2011/03/pass-the-mic-luol-deng-wins-the-most-underrated-player-award/ Pass the Mic: Luol Deng wins the Most Underrated Player Award] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110405073141/http://dimemag.com/2011/03/pass-the-mic-luol-deng-wins-the-most-underrated-player-award/ |date=5 April 2011 }} on ''[[Dime Magazine]]''; Bressman, Eric (31 March 2011) Coach Thibodeau has consistently called Deng the "glue" that holds the Bulls together. "Luol's professional. He practices hard. He prepares well. He studies his opponent. He's great at executing offensively and defensively. He's helped this team get better every day," said Thibodeau.[https://www.chicagotribune.com/2011/03/14/deng-deserves-all-defensive-thibodeau/ Deng deserves All-Defensive] on ''[[Chicago Tribune]]''; Johnson, K.C. (14 March 2011) Deng was the Bulls' second leading scorer during the playoffs. In the first game of the [[NBA Conference Finals|Eastern Conference finals]] against the Miami Heat, Deng was praised for his defense on [[LeBron James]]. However, the Heat went on to eliminate the Bulls in five games.[https://www.chicagotribune.com/2011/05/16/deng-neutralizes-james/ Deng neutralizes James] on ''[[Chicago Tribune]]''; Greenstein, Teddy (16 May 2011)[http://articles.nydailynews.com/2011-05-15/sports/29566932_1_wade-and-bosh-bogans-lebron-james Derrick Rose, Luol Deng, Chicago Bulls overpower Miami Heat to take Game 1 of Eastern finals, 103–82] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120515224850/http://articles.nydailynews.com/2011-05-15/sports/29566932_1_wade-and-bosh-bogans-lebron-james |date=15 May 2012 }} on ''[[New York Daily News]]'' (15 May 2011) Deng averaged just under 43 minutes, 16.9 points, 6.6 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game during the 2011 playoffs.[https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/blog/ball_dont_lie/post/Video-LeBron-gives-chase-but-Deng-throws-down;_ylt=AqHFRglHP2Kw4zzcfuvD.Qf4PKB4?urn=nba-wp3947 LeBron gives chase, but Deng throws down] on ''[[Yahoo!]]'' Sports; Devine, Dan (27 May 2011) ====2011–12 season: All-Star season==== [[File:Danny Granger and Luol Deng.jpg|thumb|Deng shooting a jump shot in a game with the Bulls]] Deng injured his wrist during the fourth quarter against the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] on 21 January 2012. Initially thought to be a minor injury, it was later revealed by a [[magnetic resonance imaging]] (MRI) that Deng tore the ligament in his left wrist. He decided to postpone surgery and play the rest of the [[2011–12 NBA season|2011–12 season]] through the pain. He returned to the starting line-up against the Milwaukee Bucks on 4 February 2012, scoring 21 points with 9 rebounds, 1 steal, and 1 block.{{citation needed|date=November 2024}} On 9 February, Deng was selected as a reserve for the [[2012 NBA All-Star Game]], joining teammate Derrick Rose, who was voted in as a starter. This was the first time since 1997 (when both [[Michael Jordan]] and [[Scottie Pippen]] made the team) that the Bulls had two All-Stars in the [[NBA All-Star Game]]. Deng made a buzzer-beating game winner on 24 March, off a tip-in basket to lift the Bulls 102–101 in overtime versus the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/la-sp-nba-20120325,0,5002171.story |title=Luol Deng gives Bulls victory in overtime |author=AP |date=25 March 2012 |work=Los Angeles Times |access-date=30 March 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120329192818/http://www.latimes.com/sports/la-sp-nba-20120325,0,5002171.story |archive-date=29 March 2012 |url-status=live}} At the end of the season, Deng was selected for the [[NBA All-Defensive Second Team]]. ====2012–13 season: Second All-Star season==== Deng was selected as a reserve for the [[2013 NBA All-Star Game]], along with [[Joakim Noah]]. During the [[2012–13 NBA season|2012–13 season]], he averaged a team-high 16.5 points, 6.3 rebounds, and a career-high 3 assists per game. His free throw percentage of .816 was also a career high. He again led the league in minutes per game with (38.7). Even without Derrick Rose, who was out for the whole year due to an [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|ACL injury]], the Bulls still tallied a 45–37 record, finishing fifth in the [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|Eastern Conference]] and second in the [[Central Division (NBA)|Central Division]].{{citation needed|date=November 2024}} The Bulls met the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in the first round of the [[2013 NBA playoffs|2013 playoffs]], and defeated the Nets in seven games. They then met the Miami Heat in the conference semi-finals. The Heat defeated the Bulls in five games. The Heat went on to win the [[2013 NBA Finals]]. During the 2013 playoffs, Deng averaged 13.8 points, 7.6 rebounds, and 3.8 assists in 44.8 minutes per game. ====2013–14 season==== Deng's representatives and Bulls executives had informal talks about extending his contract over the summer, but the team never made a formal offer. Deng's contract was set to expire after the [[2013–14 NBA season|2013–14 season]], and he sought a new contract close to $12 million a year over 4–5 seasons. Rumors about him being traded continued throughout the season.{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/luol-deng-rejected--30-million-extension-offer-from-bulls-before-trade-to-cavs-073843211.html|title=Luol Deng rejected ($30) million extension offer from Bulls before trade to Cavs|publisher=Yahoo! Sports|author=Adrian Wojnarowski|date=7 January 2014|access-date=29 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181129100650/https://sports.yahoo.com/news/luol-deng-rejected--30-million-extension-offer-from-bulls-before-trade-to-cavs-073843211.html|archive-date=29 November 2018|url-status=live}} During the first months of the season, Deng again emerged as the Bulls leading scorer with the absence of Derrick Rose. He had his best performances on 27 and 30 November 2013, when he scored 27 points against the [[Detroit Pistons]] and the Cleveland Cavaliers in two separate games. He also registered six rebounds against the Pistons, and 11 assists against the Cavaliers.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/2429/luol-deng|title=Luol Deng Game by Game Stats|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=8 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140108030233/http://espn.go.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/2429/luol-deng|archive-date=8 January 2014|url-status=live}} During the first two months of the season, Deng averaged a career-high of 19 points and 3.7 assists per game, and also averaged 6.9 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/2429/luol-deng|title=Luol Deng Stats|publisher=ESPN|access-date=8 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140108030221/http://espn.go.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/2429/luol-deng|archive-date=8 January 2014|url-status=live}} ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2014)=== On 7 January 2014, the Chicago Bulls traded Deng to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] for [[Andrew Bynum]], two future second-round draft picks in [[2015 NBA draft|2015]] and [[2016 NBA draft|2016]] (initially traded from the Trail Blazers to the Cavaliers), a protected future pick the Cavaliers received from the [[Sacramento Kings]], and the right to swap first-round picks with the Cavaliers in the 2015 draft.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/deng-trade-140107|title=Cavs Acquire Luol Deng from Bulls|date=7 January 2014|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=7 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140107111333/http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/deng-trade-140107|archive-date=7 January 2014|url-status=live}} At the time of the trade, Deng was the fifth-longest tenured Bulls player, and fourth-leading scorer in franchise history.{{cite web|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/basketball/bulls/chi-luol-deng-andrew-bynum-trade-bulls-20140106,0,4004271.story|title=Bulls trade Luol Deng to Cavaliers for Andrew Bynum, draft picks|date=7 January 2014|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|access-date=7 January 2014|archive-url=https://archive.today/20140107150420/http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/basketball/bulls/chi-luol-deng-andrew-bynum-trade-bulls-20140106,0,4004271.story|archive-date=7 January 2014|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}} In his Cavaliers debut, Deng had 10 points, one rebound, one steal, and four turnovers in 21 minutes.{{cite web|title=Cavs cool off Jazz in Luol Deng's debut with Cleveland|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/id/400489412/gameId/400489412/cleveland-cavaliers-vs-utah-jazz|website=[[ESPN]]|agency=Associated Press|access-date=10 February 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150108170933/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap/_/id/400489412/gameId/400489412/cleveland-cavaliers-vs-utah-jazz|archive-date=8 January 2015|url-status=live}} Two games later, he scored 27 points with five rebounds, four assists, and one block. This was his highest-scoring game with the Cavaliers.{{cite web|url=http://stats.nba.com/game/#!/0021300565/|title=Game Summary Boxscore: Cavs 120, Lakers 118|work=NBA.com|date=14 January 2014|access-date=9 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150508221129/http://stats.nba.com/game/#!/0021300565/|archive-date=8 May 2015|url-status=live}} Deng finished the season averaging 14.1 points and 2.5 assists. ===Miami Heat (2014–2016)=== On 15 July 2014, Deng signed with the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite news |title=HEAT Signs Luol Deng |date=15 July 2014 |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-luol-deng |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140717095628/http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-luol-deng |archive-date=17 July 2014 |url-status=live }} He had his best scoring game of the [[2014–15 NBA season|2014–15 season]] on 20 January 2015, when he scored 29 points against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. Deng finished the season averaging 14 points and 5.2 rebounds per game. On 29 June 2015, Deng exercised his player option for the [[2015–16 NBA season|2015–16 season]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/luol-deng-exercises-player-option|title=Luol Deng Exercises Player Option|date=29 June 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=29 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150702032256/http://www.nba.com/heat/news/luol-deng-exercises-player-option|archive-date=2 July 2015|url-status=live}} On 1 August, Deng played for Team Africa at the [[NBA Africa Game 2015|2015 NBA Africa exhibition game]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13359599/nba-current-former-stars-put-show-africa-exhibition |title=NBA stars, legends shine as Team World rallies to beat Team Africa |date=August 2015 |access-date=3 August 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150803065105/http://espn.go.com/nba/story/_/id/13359599/nba-current-former-stars-put-show-africa-exhibition |archive-date=3 August 2015 |url-status=live}} In late November and early December 2015, Deng missed six games with a left hamstring strain.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151209/MIACHA/gameinfo.html |title=Hornets beat Heat 99–81 for third straight victory |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=10 December 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151209202756/http://www.nba.com/games/20151209/MIACHA/gameinfo.html |archive-date=9 December 2015 |url-status=live}} On 19 February 2016, he scored a season-high 30 points in a 115–111 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160219/MIAATL/gameinfo.html |title=Deng has 30 points, short-handed Heat beat Hawks 115–111 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=20 February 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160221031202/http://www.nba.com/games/20160219/MIAATL/gameinfo.html |archive-date=21 February 2016 |url-status=live}} The Heat finished the regular season as the third seed in the Eastern Conference with a 48–34 record. In the first round of the [[2016 NBA playoffs|2016 playoffs]], the Heat faced the sixth-seeded [[Charlotte Hornets]], and in a game 1 win on 17 April, Deng set a Heat playoff debut record with 31 points on 11-for-13 shooting.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160417/CHAMIA/gameinfo.html|title=Deng scores 31 points, Heat rout Hornets 123–91 in Game 1|work=NBA.com|date=17 April 2016|access-date=18 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160417230131/http://www.nba.com/games/20160417/CHAMIA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=17 April 2016|url-status=live}} ===Los Angeles Lakers (2016–2018)=== On 7 July 2016, Deng signed a four-year, $72 million contract with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/160707clarksondengzubac|title=Lakers Sign Clarkson, Deng, and Zubac|work=NBA.com|date=7 July 2016|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160711063829/http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/160707clarksondengzubac|archive-date=11 July 2016}} The Lakers signed the two-time All-Star along with [[Timofey Mozgov]] to big contracts in a bid to remain competitive after [[Kobe Bryant]]'s recent retirement. However, in February 2017, [[Magic Johnson]] became the Lakers' president of basketball operations, and coach [[Luke Walton]] benched Deng to start rookie [[Brandon Ingram]].{{cite news|last=Ganguli|first=Tania|title=Lakers part ways with Luol Deng, clearing salary cap space for next summer|date=1 September 2018|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/la-sp-lakers-luol-deng-waived-20180901-story.html|access-date=3 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180902210029/http://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/la-sp-lakers-luol-deng-waived-20180901-story.html|archive-date=2 September 2018|url-status=live}}{{cite web|last=Plaschke|first=Bill|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/la-sp-lakers-deng-plaschke-20180210-story.html|title=Lakers' Luol Deng tries to make do trapped in his nowhere land|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|date=10 February 2018|access-date=11 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180210234616/http://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/la-sp-lakers-deng-plaschke-20180210-story.html|archive-date=10 February 2018|url-status=live}} He missed the final 22 games of the [[2016–17 NBA season|2016–17 season]] after being shut down in March to give more playing time to the team's young players.{{cite web|last=Shelburne|first=Ramona|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/18911909/los-angeles-lakers-shut-luol-deng-timofey-mozgov-remainder-season|title=Sources: Healthy Luol Deng, Timofey Mozgov agree to sit out rest of Lakers' season|work=ESPN.com|date=15 March 2017|access-date=15 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170315173132/http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/18911909/los-angeles-lakers-shut-luol-deng-timofey-mozgov-remainder-season|archive-date=15 March 2017|url-status=live}} On opening night of the [[2017–18 NBA season|2017–18 season]], Deng made a substitute start in place of a suspended [[Kentavious Caldwell-Pope]]; it was the only game he played the entire season. He and head coach Walton mutually decided that it was better for him to stay in the locker room during games than to play meaningless minutes in [[garbage time]]. On 1 September 2018, he was waived and stretched by the Lakers after reaching a buyout agreement.{{cite web |title=Lakers Waive Luol Deng |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/180901waive-deng |website=NBA.com |access-date=1 September 2018 |date=1 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180901220159/https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/180901waive-deng |archive-date=1 September 2018 |url-status=live}} The move freed him to find playing time elsewhere, while the Lakers gained [[NBA salary cap|salary cap]] space to potentially offer a maximum contract to a free agent in 2019.{{cite web |last1=Wojnarowski |first1=Adrian |last2=Shelburne |first2=Ramona |title=Luol Deng gives back $7.5M in buyout agreement with Lakers |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/24547748/luol-deng-agrees-75m-give-back-contract-buyout-los-angeles-lakers |website=ESPN.com |access-date=1 September 2018 |date=1 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180902065859/http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/24547748/luol-deng-agrees-75m-give-back-contract-buyout-los-angeles-lakers |archive-date=2 September 2018 |url-status=live}} Deng had been the highest-paid Laker in each of his two seasons. ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2018–2019)=== On 10 September 2018, Deng signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], reuniting him with [[Derrick Rose]], [[Jimmy Butler]], [[Taj Gibson]], and head coach [[Tom Thibodeau]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-luol-deng|title=TIMBERWOLVES SIGN LUOL DENG|work=NBA.com|date=10 September 2018|access-date=10 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180911011219/https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-luol-deng|archive-date=11 September 2018|url-status=live}} On 11 February 2019, Deng started in place of an ill [[Andrew Wiggins]] and scored 12 points in a 130–120 win against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. It was Deng's first start since 19 October 2017, his lone game for the Lakers during the [[2017–18 NBA season|2017–18 season]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071518|title=Healthy Rose, Teague lead Timberwolves past Clippers 130–120|work=ESPN.com|date=11 February 2019|access-date=12 February 2019}} Deng's final NBA game was played on February 27, 2019, in a 131–123 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. In his final game, Deng recorded one rebound and one steal in eight minutes of playing time.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/201902270ATL.html|title=Minnesota Timberwolves at Atlanta Hawks Box Score, February 27, 2019|publisher=[[Sports Reference|Basketball Reference]]|access-date=July 20, 2026}} He would go on to sign a one-day contract with the Bulls to retire with the team.{{cite web |title=Bulls sign Luol Deng, who retires from NBA after 15 seasons |url=https://www.nba.com/news/chicago-bulls-sign-luol-deng-who-will-retire |website=NBA.com |access-date=18 November 2024 |date=17 October 2019}} ==National team career== Deng represented England at [[England men's national under-16 basketball team|under-16]] and [[England men's national under-18 basketball team|under-19]] levels, and was an [[ambassador]] for the [[2012 Summer Olympics]].
